newsitem.title: USA: Rubin to de-emphasize strong dlr - US business chief.
newsitem.headline: Rubin to de-emphasize strong dlr - US business chief.

text.p: The Clinton administration is likely to de-emphasize the importance of a strong dollar for the U.S. economy as growth slows, the head of the National Association of Manufacturers said Thursday.
"As the economy slows, Treasury Secretary (Robert) Rubin will be saying less about the value of a strong dollar," Association President Jerry Jasinowski told reporters.
But he added that he does not expect Rubin to start "talking down the dollar."
Jasinowski said he expects the dollar to "taper off a little bit" as U.S. economic growth slows and long-term interest rates ease.
Growth will pick up to an annualized rate of about 2.5 percent in the fourth quarter, but then it will fall to below two percent in the first quarter of next year, he said.

The economy grew at a 2.2 percent annual clip in the third quarter. Jasinowski forecast a reasonably successful Christmas selling season, arguing that growth in personal income should buoy consumer outlays.
But then he sees consumer spending slowing down again in the first quarter of next year.
